channel.title: Carat Capital — The Trade Paper of the Jewelry World
channel.description: Prices, intelligence and analysis from every desk of the stone trade: diamonds, gold and metals, gemstones, watches, auctions, retail and technology.

item.title: Four times its metal: a Garrard egg makes £123,500
item.description: A 22-carat gold Cadbury 'Conundrum' egg by Garrard sold for £123,500, about $166,600, at Batemans on 1 August. That is close to six times its estimate and roughly four times the melt value of its 323.6 grams.

item.title: 640,000 ounces: China's biggest gold month since 2023
item.description: The People's Bank of China added 640,000 troy ounces in July, about 19.9 tonnes and the largest single month since October 2023. Holdings reached 76.08 million ounces, roughly 2,366 tonnes, in a 21st consecutive month of buying.

item.title: 938 at the exchange, 1,286 at the counter
item.description: Shanghai Gold Exchange Au99.99 traded at 938 yuan a gram on 8 August, up 7.53 on the day. Chow Tai Fook's 24-carat counter read 1,286 yuan, a spread of 348 yuan a gram, about 37% over the benchmark.

item.title: Turkey +6.9%, America −14.8%: where Swiss watches went
item.description: Swiss watch exports to Turkey rose 6.9% to 165.2 million francs in the first half. Shipments to the United States fell 14.8%, Germany 10.5% and China 5.0%. India rose 31.5% and Mexico 14.9%.

item.title: 46% of Kalyan's revenue came back through the door
item.description: Kalyan Jewellers took ₹10,589 crore of revenue in the June quarter, up 46%, and net profit of ₹349 crore, up 32%. Recycled gold supplied more than 46% of revenue and more than 55% in June alone.

item.title: P.N. Gadgil retires Litestyle and bets on 100 YOOU stores
item.description: P N Gadgil Jewellers replaced its lightweight diamond line Litestyle with a new brand, YOOU, on 8 August. It runs 13 exclusive outlets and shop-in-shop counters across five states, against a target of 100 stores by 2030.

item.title: The 106,000 jobs that weren't: payrolls miss puts gold at $4,341.30
item.description: July payrolls fell 23,000 against a consensus of about 83,000, a miss of 106,000. Gold closed Friday at $4,341.30, up $102.00 or 2.41%. September hike odds fell to 46% from 55% on the print.

item.title: Gold kept $26.80, platinum gave back $29.00: the settle against the spike
item.description: This paper marked all four metals at 5:58am on Friday. By the 5:00pm close gold had added a further $26.80, while platinum gave back $29.00, palladium $25.00 and silver $0.83. Only gold improved on its morning mark.

item.title: $13,000 for costume, £2,000 for gold: Bonhams runs Chanel in three cities
item.description: Bonhams will hold three Chanel sales in September: New York 7 to 17, Paris 14 to 24 with about 400 lots, London 21 September to 1 October. The top jewellery lot is a 1960 Goossens bangle at $13,000 to $20,000.

item.title: 29% said diamond, 57% said fashion jewellery: Hong Kong's two answers
item.description: HKTDC surveyed 1,507 buyers and exhibitors at its twin Hong Kong shows, 29 July to 2 August. Diamond led demand at 29%, ruby 25%, pearl 20%. Trendy fashion jewellery led growth potential at 57%, precious jewellery 35%.

item.title: Up 8.6% in dollars, down in units: the $1,500 line splits the counter
item.description: Tenoris data puts US jewellery sales up 8.6% in the first half on a 19% rise in average purchase price and a fall in units. Sales below $1,500 kept declining. June sales rose 13% year on year.

item.title: Buyers up 5%, 96% already rebooked: Rockview's first NY Now
item.description: NY Now's summer edition ran 2 to 4 August at the Javits Center with 460 exhibitors, the first under Rockview Management Group. Buyer attendance rose 5% and 96% of exhibitors have renewed for the 31 January winter show.

item.title: Fifteen years, no tax: what Mumbai just offered to take from Dubai
item.description: India's lower house passed a Bill on 6 August exempting qualifying foreign rough sellers from income tax between 1 October 2026 and 31 March 2041. It replaces a safe harbour that presumes profit at 1.25% of gross revenue, against corporate rates reaching about 33%.

item.title: $4,314.50 and silver up 4.71%: every metal runs before payrolls
item.description: At 5:58am New York gold bid $4,314.50, up $75.20 or 1.77%. Silver added $2.89 or 4.71% to $64.29, platinum 3.14% to $1,772.00 and palladium 2.14% to $1,382.00. The ratio tightened to 67.1 from 69.3. Payrolls land at 8:30am.

item.title: 132 tonnes of jewellery, 339 tonnes of bars: China picks a side
item.description: China Gold Association figures put first-half gold jewellery consumption at 132.13 tonnes, down 33.88%, against bar and coin demand of 339.34 tonnes, up 28.42%. Total consumption still rose 1.23% to 511.41 tonnes. The jewellery counter is now the smaller half by a distance.

item.title: $2,238 an order: Brilliant Earth buys its profit back
item.description: Second-quarter revenue rose 6% to $115.1 million on 2.1% fewer orders, with average order value up 8% to $2,238. Gross margin reached 57.9% and the company posted $0.8 million of net income against a $1.1 million loss. Full-year guidance goes to $459-462 million.

item.title: The 14% that isn't a decline: platinum's China forecast, read properly
item.description: The World Platinum Investment Council projects Chinese platinum jewellery down 14% in 2026 and global platinum jewellery down 12%. Strip out an unrepeated 2025 stock build and Chinese fabrication shows a small increase. Spot platinum added 3.14% to $1,772.00 the same week.

item.title: $29.99 at the piercing counter: lab-grown finds the mass market
item.description: Claire's is rebuilding its in-store piercing service across the United States and Canada from August, its second overhaul in three years, and adding lab-grown diamond studs to the starter assortment. Kits begin at $29.99 with the piercing free.

item.title: $4,270.90, a seven-week high, and silver alone in the red
item.description: At 6:03am New York gold bid $4,270.90, up 0.58% and a fourth consecutive session higher. Platinum added 1.33% to $1,753.00 and palladium 1.48% to $1,367.00. Silver fell 0.41% to $61.67, widening the ratio to 69.3.

item.title: Alrosa books a $134 million loss and starts idling the pits
item.description: Revenue fell 36% to 74.2 billion roubles, about $932.5 million, and the world's largest rough producer swung to a net loss of 10.67 billion roubles, about $134.1 million, from a $490.1 million profit. Several open pits go to care and maintenance this year.

item.title: Signet puts 25 years of Tiffany into Blue Nile
item.description: Pam Cloud becomes president of Blue Nile on 10 August, reporting to chief operating and financial officer Joan Hilson. She spent more than 25 years at Tiffany, latterly as senior vice president and chief merchandising officer, and founded a direct-to-consumer pearl brand.

item.title: £13 billion of buy-now-pay-later is now inside the FCA's perimeter
item.description: Deferred payment credit came under Financial Conduct Authority supervision on 15 July. The market ran from £60 million of transactions in 2017 to more than £13 billion in 2024, with about 11 million British users. Lenders now owe affordability checks and Ombudsman access.

item.title: $934 million for 117 anchors: a second run at the JCPenney estate
item.description: Onyx Partners has bid $934 million for 117 J.C. Penney stores covering 15.7 million square feet across 35 states, about $8 million a store. A $947 million offer was rejected in December. The firm says financing is in place to close on 25 September.

item.title: 67% asked a chatbot: the gift search has left the search box
item.description: Attentive's survey of 600 American adults finds 67% used an AI chatbot to help them shop in the past three months, rising to 80% of Gen Z. Separately 62% will plan holiday purchases before November and 71% will start buying before Black Friday.

item.title: Four metals, third session: gold $4,157.80, silver up 3.27%
item.description: At 5:58am New York gold bid $4,157.80, up 1.99%, silver $61.35, up 3.27%, platinum $1,747.00, up 1.10% and palladium $1,355.00, up 1.96%. The gold to silver ratio tightened to 67.8.

item.title: ₹1,45,359 and rising: India confirms the metals turn at home
item.description: October gold on the MCX rose 0.73% to ₹1,45,359 per 10 grams and September silver 1.13% to ₹2,24,109 a kilo. Indian jewellery demand fell 19% in the first quarter and 15% in the second.

item.title: Twenty percent in June: Hong Kong's fourteenth month up
item.description: Jewellery, watches and clocks took HK$5.49 billion in June, up 20% year on year, inside overall retail of HK$31.49 billion, up 5%. First-half hard luxury rose 25% to HK$31.07 billion.

item.title: Six months empty: Pandora hands North America to a beauty CEO
item.description: André Branch becomes president of Pandora's North America cluster on 15 August, a seat vacant since Luciano Rodembusch left in February. He arrives from R.E.M. Beauty, with two decades in consumer brands and none in jewellery.

item.title: Fifty percent on fixed price: how Luk Fook outran the gold price
item.description: Net profit rose 88.7% to HK$2.015 billion in the year to 31 March, on revenue up 29% to HK$17.21 billion. Fixed-price jewellery sales rose 50.5% against 22% for gold and platinum by weight.

item.title: Eighty percent to the consumer: the NDC changes the subject
item.description: Amber Pepper told a GJEPC meeting in Mumbai that at least 80% of Natural Diamond Council advertising now goes to consumers, with a desire index baseline due in September and a trust mark to be inscribed on stones.
